lore.name: Open Windows with Music
lore.summary: Music drifting out of open windows is the sound of the neighbourhood, and one of the things Zed fights to bring back.
lore.body: The Theme lists open windows with music alongside corner shops and murals as the heart of a lived-in city. Zed names it in his mission: he fights so music can drift from open windows again.

lore.name: Street Tournaments and Late-Night Sparring
lore.summary: Where Zed learned to juggle, dodge and parry: street tournaments and sparring behind the corner shops.
lore.body: Zed learned to fight the way he learned to dance, through rhythm, instinct and community. The tournaments and late-night sparring behind the corner shops taught him combos and defence long before the Rust arrived.

lore.name: The Corner Shops
lore.summary: Mustard-yellow storefronts on every corner, and the backdrop for Zed's late-night sparring.
lore.body: Corner shops are the first thing the Theme names when it describes the neighbourhood. Zed's block was known for its mustard-yellow storefronts, and the space behind them is where he sparred late at night.

lore.name: Taking the City Back
lore.summary: Zed's goal: take the Fallen City back one district at a time and find out what happened to his father.
lore.body: Every wave Zed clears and every arena he survives brings him closer to the answer about his father and to restoring the community that raised him. He fights so kids can play on the courts, music can drift from open windows, and murals can rise again, celebrating real heroes.

lore.name: Zed's City Colours
lore.summary: Zed wears mustard yellow, brick red and forest green as a reminder of what he is fighting for.
lore.body: The neighbourhood palette is mustard yellow, brick red, forest green and warm browns. Zed carries the first three in his outfit, casual and expressive, so the city goes into every fight with him.

lore.name: The Quiet After the Takeover
lore.summary: After the Rust arrived, friends vanished, neighbours were hurt and the city's heartbeat went quiet.
lore.body: The GDD says friends vanished and neighbours were beaten, and the stall was seized for security violations. It stops there: it names no one and gives no further detail. This is why Zed had no choice but to fight.

lore.gddGap: The GDD says only 'Rust Enemies'. 'Rust grunt' is the working Tier 0 enemy name from the asset manifest and canon open question 6; the owner has not confirmed it as the player-facing term.
lore.name: Rust Grunt
lore.summary: The rank-and-file member of the Rust: uniformed, visored and boxy, and the one enemy type in Tier 0.
lore.body: A Rust grunt is a person in a uniform, not a monster. Cold hues, steel and a cyan visor set them apart from the warm neighbourhood. They arrive in waves, and Zed knocks them down and pushes them back.

lore.name: Zed
lore.summary: A kid from Brick-Red Alley who learned to fight the way he learned to dance, and is taking the Fallen City back one district at a time.
lore.body:
Zed grew up believing strength is about protecting the people who give your life meaning. He fights through rhythm, instinct and community, not training-ground discipline. He is expressive, stubborn and fiercely loyal, and he cracks jokes mid-fight.

He wears the city's colours, mustard yellow, brick red and forest green, as a reminder of what he is fighting for. Every wave he clears brings him closer to the community that raised him, and to finding out what happened to his father.

lore.name: Zed's Mother
lore.summary: She ran a tiny food stall by the community garden, serving hot stew to anyone who needed a meal.
lore.body:
Her stall was a gathering point for the block: nobody who was hungry went without a bowl. The Rust seized the stall for "security violations".

The GDD gives her no name and does not say where she is now.

lore.name: Zed's Father
lore.summary: A muralist who painted the faces of local heroes across the district walls; he disappeared after confronting the Rust at a mural teardown.
lore.body:
He painted cooks, musicians, activists and teachers, everyday people who kept the Fallen City standing. When the Rust came to tear down his murals, he stood up to them, and he has not been seen since.

What happened to him is the question that pulls Zed forward. The GDD leaves it open.

lore.name: The Fallen City
lore.summary: A lived-in, culturally rich city of corner shops, murals, music and community, overtaken by a corrupt private security force.
lore.body:
Before the Rust, the city was loud, hopeful and full of people who looked out for each other: corner shops, open windows with music drifting out, basketball courts, food stalls and community gardens. Its colours are mustard yellow, brick red, forest green and warm browns.

It is made of districts, and Zed means to take it back one district at a time.

lore.name: Brick-Red Alley
lore.summary: The alley where the neighbourhood kids learned to fight, dance and argue like family.
lore.body:
Zed's home block is known for its mustard-yellow storefronts, forest-green basketball courts and this brick-red alley. It was not perfect, but it was alive.

The Rust now patrol the alleys where kids used to play.

lore.name: The Food Stall
lore.summary: Zed's mother's tiny stall near the community garden, serving hot bowls of stew to anyone who needed one.
lore.body: A small, warm centre of the block. Seized by the Rust for "security violations", it stands for the food stalls Zed fights to bring back.

lore.name: The Community Garden
lore.summary: A shared garden beside the food stall, fenced off when the Rust took over.
lore.body: The garden belonged to everyone on the block. The Rust fenced it off, and reopening it is part of giving the neighbourhood its heartbeat back.

lore.name: The Basketball Courts
lore.summary: Forest-green courts where the block played, shut down by the Rust.
lore.body: Part of Zed's block and of the city's everyday life. Zed fights so kids can play on them again.

lore.name: The Local Heroes Murals
lore.summary: Murals across the district walls celebrating everyday heroes: cooks, musicians, activists and teachers.
lore.body:
Painted largely by Zed's father, the murals told the city's stories. The Rust tore them down, his included, and put surveillance towers and propaganda screens in their place.

Zed fights so murals can rise again, celebrating real heroes.

lore.name: Surveillance Towers and Propaganda Screens
lore.summary: What the Rust put up where the murals used to be.
lore.body: Cold, boxy and official, they are the opposite of a painted wall. They show the Rust watching the neighbourhood instead of belonging to it.

lore.name: The Neighbourhood
lore.summary: Zed's side: ordinary people who look out for each other, warm, casual and expressive.
lore.body: Cooks, musicians, teachers, kids and neighbours in casual fits and expressive colours. They answer the Rust with paint, music and plain stubbornness.

lore.name: The Rust
lore.summary: A corrupt private security force that swept through the districts and overtook the Fallen City.
lore.body:
The Rust did not arrive like soldiers; they arrived like thieves. They shut the courts, fenced the gardens, patrolled the alleys and tore down the murals. They are uniformed, symmetrical, visored and cold, and their ordinary members are the Rust grunts Zed knocks back in each arena.

They are people in a force, not a place or a stain, and the neighbourhood always has an answer for them.

lore.name: The Takeover
lore.summary: The day everything changed: the Rust swept through the districts and the city's heartbeat went quiet.
lore.body:
Courts were shut, gardens fenced, murals torn down and stalls seized. Zed's father disappeared confronting the Rust at a mural teardown, and friends vanished.

Zed did not have a choice. He had to fight.

lore.gddGap: The GDD's campaign table names the Level 6 district 'Iron-line-push' and the Level 6 mini-boss and boss arena (an undercity lab), but never describes the district. The look and story here are derived from the Level 6 style guide and the Holt arena line.
lore.name: Iron Line Push
lore.summary: Level 6 district: the undercity, where the Rust push their line down below the streets and Dr. Holt's lab keeps the air heavy.
lore.body:
The Iron Line Push is Level 6 in the GDD's campaign table. Its mini-boss is Dr. Holt's Experiment, Subject 88, and its boss is Overseer Dr. Maren Holt, whose arena the GDD describes as an undercity lab with gas vents, toxin pools and fog zones. The name echoes the Rust Grunts, the Iron Line, who are the backbone of the force.

Here the neighbourhood's warmth is hardest to find. The stew pots and the stalls are far overhead, and down below the Rust have run their line of barriers through the tunnels, with Watchers and Breakers behind it. The way through is clear air: every vent shut, every fog bank crossed, one careful step at a time.

The Level 6 style guide still shows a stall-row garden look from an earlier pass; this entry follows the GDD's undercity wording and the style guide will need to catch up. Zed's neighbours are watching from the edges of the lane in spirit, not in sight: the hope in this district is the daylight at the far end.

lore.gddGap: The GDD's campaign table names the Level 7 district 'Copper-fang-courts' and its mini-boss, Commander Atlas, but gives no description. The main boss, 'Elite Rust Gauntlet', is named only; the owner will define it later, so nothing about it is invented here.
lore.name: Copper Fang Courts
lore.summary: Level 7 district: the forest-green courts, now a Copper Fang stronghold, where Commander Atlas stands between the kids and their game.
lore.body:
The Copper Fang Courts are Level 7 in the GDD's campaign table. Commander Atlas, leader of the Copper Fangs and the toughest non-boss enemy in the game, is the mini-boss. The GDD lists the level's main boss as the Elite Rust Gauntlet and gives no more detail yet, so this entry leaves it open.

It grows out of the Greenline Courts, the forest-green basketball courts that the Rust shut down at the start of the takeover. The Copper Fangs, Varr's personal favourites, now hold the courts as a command post: the hoops are bent but standing, chalk drawings from the kids still show on the asphalt, and a cold slate tent sits at centre court.

The fight is about holding your nerve against disciplined, shielded opponents. When the Fangs are pushed back, the first sound should be a ball bouncing on the asphalt, then another.

lore.gddGap: The GDD's campaign table names the Level 8 district 'Overseer-tower' with Sentinel-X9 and Halden Varr, and the Varr arena as a corporate tower command chamber. It does not describe the rest of the tower; the climb and the skyline are derived from the Level 8 style guide.
lore.name: Overseer Tower
lore.summary: Level 8, the final district: the corporate tower from which Overseer Halden Varr runs the whole Fallen City.
lore.body:
The Overseer Tower is Level 8 in the GDD's campaign table. Its mini-boss is Sentinel-X9, an experimental combat android protecting Varr, and its boss is Overseer Halden Varr, The Architect of Rust. The GDD places his arena in the tower's command chamber.

From the Heights the tower is the one cold shape on the skyline: grey slate against a warm dusk, with a single cyan eye watching the windows that used to play music. Squads, drones and shields answer to Varr from here, and the screens and surveillance towers seen in every other district are fed from this room.

For Zed it is the last stop on taking the Fallen City back. The hope is plain: break the order in the command chamber and the music can come back into the windows.

lore.name: "Brick" Dugan
lore.summary: Level 1 mini-boss: a former dock worker recruited into the Rust, built like a human battering ram.
lore.body:
Brick Dugan is the mini-boss of Level 1. The GDD calls him a former dock worker who was recruited into the Rust. He wears a heavy black security vest with the Rust insignia, riot-control shoulder pads, reinforced forearm guards and steel-toe security boots, with a utility belt carrying restraints and radio equipment.

His moves are the Brick Breaker Punch, a Running Shoulder Charge, a Ground Stomp, a Grab and Wall Slam, and a Rage Punch when his health is low. The GDD wants him to feel like a human battering ram: slow but intimidating, easy to understand but hard to face head-on, and the player's first major skill check.

lore.name: "Railgun" Royce
lore.summary: Level 2 mini-boss in the Transit District: a former transit security officer who introduces stun mechanics.
lore.body:
Railgun Royce is the mini-boss of Level 2, the Transit District. The GDD describes him as a former transit security officer. He carries an electrified baton, wears an armoured trench coat and sees through a scanner visor.

His moves are a Baton Combo, a Charging Dash, a Shockwave Slam, a Rail Trap (electrified floor sections) and a Taser Burst. His role in the game is to introduce stun mechanics.

lore.name: "Crusher" Kane
lore.summary: Level 3 mini-boss in the Industrial Zone: Rhea Calder's chief enforcer, in a hydraulic work suit with an industrial hammer.
lore.body:
Crusher Kane is the mini-boss of Level 3, the Industrial Zone, and the GDD names him Rhea Calder's chief enforcer. He fights in a hydraulic work suit and swings an industrial hammer.

His moves are a Hammer Slam, a Hook Chain Grab, a Furnace Kick, a Steam Vent Burst and a Crushing Uppercut. His role is to prepare players for Overseer Calder.

lore.name: "Glitch"
lore.summary: Level 4 mini-boss in the Neon Market: a former hacker turned Rust cyber operative who introduces Voss's deception mechanics.
lore.body:
Glitch is the mini-boss of Level 4, the Neon Market. The GDD describes a former hacker turned Rust cyber operative, wearing a holographic mask and a portable drone pack.

His moves are a Drone Barrage, a Hologram Duplicate, a Shock Disk Throw, a Data Spike and an Emergency Teleport. His role is to introduce Overseer Voss's deception mechanics.

lore.name: "Raptor"
lore.summary: Level 5 mini-boss in the Skyline District: Silas Wren's personal hunter, who trains players for vertical combat.
lore.body:
Raptor is the mini-boss of Level 5, the Skyline District, and the GDD calls him Silas Wren's personal hunter. He fights with a grapple launcher and lightweight armour.

His moves are a Dive Kick, a Wall Bounce Strike, a Grapple Pull, an Aerial Barrage and a Falcon Drop. His role is to train players for vertical combat.

lore.name: Dr. Holt's Experiment "Subject 88"
lore.summary: Level 6 mini-boss in the Undercity: a failed chemical test subject who introduces area denial hazards.
lore.body:
Subject 88 is the mini-boss of Level 6, the Undercity. The GDD describes a failed chemical test subject of Dr. Holt's, with a mutated physique, chemical tanks on the back and glowing green veins.

Its moves are Toxic Breath, Acid Spit, a Frenzied Charge, a Corrosion Slam and a Chemical Explosion. Its role is to introduce area denial hazards.

lore.name: Commander Atlas
lore.summary: Level 7 mini-boss at the Rust Military Compound: leader of the Copper Fangs and the toughest non-boss enemy in the game.
lore.body:
Commander Atlas is the mini-boss of Level 7, the Rust Military Compound, and the GDD names him leader of the Copper Fangs. He wears elite black armour, carries a tactical shield and fights with twin electrified gauntlets.

His moves are a Shield Bash, a Gauntlet Combo, a Grapple Hook Pull, an Electric Counter and Fang Protocol, which calls in Specialists. The GDD calls him the toughest non-boss enemy in the game.

lore.name: Sentinel-X9
lore.summary: Level 8 mini-boss in the Corporate Tower: an experimental combat android protecting Varr, the final challenge before the boss.
lore.body:
Sentinel-X9 is the mini-boss of Level 8, the Corporate Tower. The GDD describes an experimental combat android protecting Varr: a corporate security robot with the Rust insignia and an energy core in its chest.

Its moves are a Laser Sweep, a Rocket Punch, a Ground Pound, an Energy Shield and a Self-Repair Mode. In Phase 2 the core overloads, bringing faster attacks, a red laser barrage and explosive dash attacks. It is the final challenge before Halden Varr.

lore.gddGap: The menu design doc shows a poster 'Rust Notice 114 / CURFEW' but the main GDD never says the Rust issue curfews or numbered notices (canon open question 1). Kept as flavour pending owner approval.
lore.name: Rust Notice 114
lore.summary: A cold, official curfew notice the Rust post on walls, always crossed out by the neighbourhood.
lore.body: Brick red and bossy, it is the Rust's way of speaking to the block. Somebody always gets to it first with a hand-inked cross-out.

lore.gddGap: The menu poster 'Local Heroes Benefit: Keep the Lights On' implies community fundraising events, which the GDD does not describe.
lore.name: Local Heroes Benefit
lore.summary: A neighbourhood benefit night, Keep the Lights On, that keeps the community together under the Rust.
lore.body: Posters for it turn up on the walls the Rust have not yet cleaned. It is proof the block is still looking out for each other.

lore.gddGap: The GDD says 'urban districts' but names none. Built from the mustard-yellow storefronts and corner shops of the Theme.
lore.name: Mustard Row
lore.summary: The shopfront street of mustard-yellow corner shops, where the first arena could sit.
lore.body: Awnings, hand-lettered signs and shutters the Rust have chained down. Reopening a shop here is the first small win.

lore.gddGap: No districts are named in the GDD. Built from the forest-green basketball courts of Zed's block.
lore.name: Greenline Courts
lore.summary: The forest-green court district, shut down and waiting for kids to come back.
lore.body: Chain-link, faded lines and a hoop with no net. When the Rust are pushed back, the first sound should be a bouncing ball.

lore.gddGap: No districts are named in the GDD. Built from the food stalls and community gardens of the Theme and Zed's mother's stall.
lore.name: Stewpot Gardens
lore.summary: Food stalls and fenced-off community gardens, the warmest corner of the city.
lore.body: Stall awnings, planters behind Rust fencing and the memory of stew. Reclaiming it means the smell of dinner is back.

lore.gddGap: No districts are named in the GDD. Built from the open windows with music and the murals celebrating local heroes.
lore.name: Songwindow Heights
lore.summary: Tall apartment blocks where music used to drift from open windows, now watched by Rust towers.
lore.body: Mural walls rise between the buildings, mostly painted over. It is the district where the music comes back.

lore.name: Zed's Rage
lore.summary: Zed's rage is born of the Rust's false promises, his father's disappearance and his willingness to fight for his city.
lore.body:
The Rage spec gives Zed's rage three roots: the Rust's false promises, the disappearance of his father, and Zed's own willingness to fight for his city. The Rust are the source of it, which is why every Rust enemy feeds it.

The father's story is only implied. The spec leaves it for cutscenes and dialogue to reveal, so nothing about what happened to him is stated here.

lore.name: The Rage Meter
lore.summary: A meter that fills as Zed lands blows on Rust enemies, from Level 2 onward, and starts fresh every level.
lore.body:
From Level 2 onward Zed's Rage builds with every blow he lands on a Rust enemy, bosses included. Light, heavy or jump kick, each blow counts the same. Misses give nothing, and a knockdown or a finishing blow adds no extra.

The meter starts empty at the beginning of every level and on a retry. Nothing carries over from one fight to the next. Level 1 is the pace level: the meter is hidden there and cannot fill.

lore.name: Staying Clean
lore.summary: Landing blows without taking a hit in between builds Rage faster; a hit ends the streak.
lore.body:
The spec rewards aggressive, clean play. Blows landed without a hit taken in between add a bonus to the meter, and taking a hit ends the streak.

Sloppy play is never locked out of Rage. It only takes longer to get there.

lore.name: Rage Ready
lore.summary: When the meter is full, Rage is READY and holds for a short window before it starts to fade.
lore.body:
A full meter means Rage is READY. It holds there for a 4-second window so Zed can finish what he is doing and answer with the L button. If the window passes, the meter starts to drain and has to be built again.

The meter drains on a timer the whole time, fighting or not, and pauses for the pause menu, wave transitions and cutscenes.

lore.name: Zed Rage
lore.summary: Zed Rage is the Special: the release of Zed's rage, a refusal to let his city fall.
lore.body:
The Special move is called Zed Rage. While Rage is active, Zed's normal attacks are replaced by this one move. The spec calls it the release of his rage, a refusal to let his city fall. It is just a move: it carries no story about Zed's father.

The Special hits hard but never finishes a boss on its own. Zed still moves, jumps and blocks during Rage, and there is no dodge. It is triggered with L.

lore.name: When the Rage Settles
lore.summary: Rage lasts a short, fixed time and ends when the meter runs out or Zed is knocked out; his normal moves return.
lore.body:
Rage runs for 9 seconds on a fixed clock. Nothing Zed does speeds it up or slows it down. It ends when the meter reaches zero, or straight away if Zed is knocked out. A knockdown from a hit does not end it.

Afterwards his normal moves come back, and the meter has to be built again from the start by landing blows on Rust enemies.

lore.gddGap: The spec names the roots of Zed's rage but not how it feels to him or how it fits his warm character. Proposed so rage reads as determination for his neighbourhood, not hatred, matching the Theme and Zed's loyalty.
lore.name: Not Hatred, Not a Grudge
lore.summary: Zed's rage is determination for the people and places he is fighting to get back, and it never makes him cruel.
lore.body:
Zed is stubborn and fiercely loyal, and his rage is the same loyalty turned all the way up. It is not about the Rust as people. It is about the courts, the stall, the murals and the music that were taken from his neighbourhood.

Even at its loudest he keeps his feet moving and knocks his opponents down, never worse. The neighbourhood would recognise it as him, only louder.

Zed is silent about the Rage: he never speaks or jokes about it, in or out of Zed Rage. It shows in the move, the meter and the music, not in his lines.

lore.gddGap: The art direction hints that grief turns to fire but gives no in-world description of how Rage looks or feels. Proposed wording for art and dialogue, built on that hint and the Theme palette.
lore.name: Grief Turning to Fire
lore.summary: When Rage builds, people on the block see Zed's grief warm into something bright and steady, like a stove coming up to heat.
lore.body:
The spec lets the art hint at the loss behind the Rage, with grief turning to fire: an ember glow that climbs toward orange and a red-white heat as the meter fills, with a stronger light in his eyes and fists once Rage is active.

In the world this is the warmth of the neighbourhood, not a threat. The people who feel it describe it as the kitchen light coming back on.

lore.gddGap: The spec says every Rust enemy feeds the rage but not why in the world. Proposed explanation: each pushed-back Rust enemy is a reminder of what the neighbourhood is owed, not something Zed enjoys.
lore.name: Every Rust Enemy Counts
lore.summary: Each Rust enemy Zed meets, from Grunts to Overseers, stirs the same rage, because they all stand for the same false promise.
lore.body:
The Rust offered protection and delivered curfews, fences and sealed districts. Every Grunt, Breaker, Watcher, Copper Fang and Overseer stands in front of Zed as a piece of that broken promise, so every blow he lands on them stirs the rage a little.

It rises from standing his ground, not from enjoying a fight. Finishing a fight adds nothing extra; landing blows is what feeds it, which fits a Zed who knocks his opponents down and moves on.

lore.gddGap: The spec says the meter drains constantly, even when full, but gives no in-world reason. Proposed: rage is a feeling Zed has to keep earning, like holding a breath, which he does not want to carry forever.
lore.name: Held Like a Breath
lore.summary: Zed cannot hold his rage for long; it fades unless he keeps earning it by standing his ground.
lore.body:
Rage is not a switch Zed can leave on. It fades if he stops fighting for his block, even when it is full, and he has about a few seconds to answer it before it settles again. That is how the neighbourhood tells it: you can't hoard a feeling like that.

When it settles he is still Zed, a bit out of breath, and ready to start building it again from his own steady footing.

lore.gddGap: The spec hides the meter in Level 1 and introduces it in Level 2 but does not say what changes in the story. Proposed: Level 1 is Zed finding his feet at home; the rage only wakes once he leaves Brick-Red Alley and the stakes grow.
lore.name: Why It Wakes in Level Two
lore.summary: In Level 1 Zed is at home and finding his rhythm; the rage first wakes as the fight moves beyond the alley.
lore.body:
Level 1 is the pace level, where Zed learns to move, chain his hits, kick from a jump and block, with nothing extra pressing on him. In the story that is Zed on his own street, steady and focused.

From Level 2 the fight spreads across more of the city, and the rage meter slides into view with a one-time prompt to explain it. The idea is that Zed feels it properly for the first time once he is further from home.

lore.name: How the Rust Got Their Foot in the Door
lore.summary: The Rust began as a private security contractor hired to steady the Fallen City, then stayed and became a militarized occupation.
lore.body:
After years of political decay and rising crime, the city hired a private security contractor to calm things down. Once the Rust were inside, they never left. The Rust transformed from a protective force into a militarized occupation, tightening their control over every district and crushing resistance with brutal efficiency.

The name comes from their oxidized metal armour, rough and weathered. The neighbourhood reads it as a reminder of what the Rust have done to the city, and Zed reads it as a challenge.

lore.name: Overseer Halden Varr, The Architect of Rust
lore.summary: The former military strategist who founded the Rust and believes order only comes through fear.
lore.body:
Varr saw the Fallen City's government collapse and saw his chance. He offered "protection" to the officials who were left, then quietly swapped them for Rust loyalists. From that day the Rust were the law.

He is the face of the Rust's cold, official voice. The Copper Fangs are his personal favourites, and the Overseers, his inner circle, run the districts in his name. He is an Overseer himself, "The Architect of Rust", and the main boss.

lore.name: Within Months: Curfews, Sealed Districts and Drones
lore.summary: Curfews became mandatory, districts were sealed, drones filled the sky and people who spoke up went missing.
lore.body:
It took the Rust only months. Curfews became mandatory. Whole districts were sealed off. Surveillance drones filled the sky. Anyone who resisted disappeared. The Rust became the law, and then they became the city.

This is the wider picture behind what Zed saw on his own block: the shut courts, the fenced gardens and the torn-down murals.

lore.name: Order is Strength. Freedom is Weakness.
lore.summary: The single doctrine the Rust live by: rebuild the Fallen City through force, suppress civilians and eliminate rebels.
lore.body:
"Order is strength. Freedom is weakness." That is the Rust's whole creed. They hold that the Fallen City can only be rebuilt by force, and that civilians are assets to be managed rather than neighbours to look after.

They are enforcers, hunters and executioners. Each unit is trained to suppress civilians, eliminate rebels and maintain absolute control, and to see rebels, Zed included, as threats to the "greater good". The neighbourhood's answer is on every wall that gets repainted: strength is looking out for each other.

lore.name: Serial Numbers
lore.summary: The Rust take away recruits' names and give them serial numbers, so nobody stands out and everyone obeys.
lore.body:
A new recruit hands over their name and gets a number. Helmets hide their faces on top of that. It wipes out who they were and keeps them in line.

It also means the person under the visor is somebody's neighbour, and nobody in the Fallen City can tell which one.

lore.name: Rust Grunts: The Iron Line
lore.summary: The backbone of the Rust: ordinary citizens pressed into service, in cheap rust-coated plating and anonymous helmets.
lore.body:
The Iron Line were once ordinary citizens, coerced or talked into joining. Their plating is cheap and rust-coated, and their helmets hide who they are on purpose. Each carries a serial number instead of a name.

They are the crowd the Rust put in front: they keep the streets under watch, make a show of force and hold the front. Zed meets them in nearly every wave.

lore.name: Rust Bruisers: The Breakers
lore.summary: Hulking enforcers in heavy plating, boosted with illegal muscle stimulants that make them strong and unsteady.
lore.body:
The Breakers are big, with reinforced plating that gives them a hulking outline. Many were once in trouble with the law and were promised their freedom in exchange for loyalty. The Rust boost them with stimulants, which makes them stronger and shaky.

The Rust use them as shock troops for area denial and for crushing resistance groups.

lore.name: Rust Rangers: The Watchers
lore.summary: Agile units with taser rifles, batons and tracking visors who chase rebels over alleys and rooftops.
lore.body:
The Watchers are quick and quiet. They carry taser rifles and batons, and their tracking visors read heat, which makes hiding hard. They are trained to follow rebels through the alleys and across the rooftops.

Their job is to harass from a distance, give chase and report back. Brick-Red Alley knows its rooftops better than they do.

lore.name: Rust Specialists: The Copper Fangs
lore.summary: Elite Rust soldiers with electrified gauntlets, grappling hooks and tactical shields, and Varr's personal favourites.
lore.body:
The Copper Fangs are picked from the most loyal Rust members and put through psychological conditioning to remove fear and hesitation. Their kit is the best the Rust have: electrified gauntlets, grappling hooks and tactical shields.

They are Overseer Varr's favourites and are sent on high-priority target elimination, which makes them mini-boss material in the arena.

lore.name: Rust Overseers: The Architects of Control
lore.summary: District bosses and strategic masterminds, Varr's inner circle, who hold their districts through surveillance, fear and psychological control.
lore.body:
The Overseers are the Rust's district bosses, strategic masterminds and Varr's inner circle. Each holds a district through surveillance, fear and psychological domination, in a tactical, oppressive style with its own tricks. They are the end-of-level bosses, the district rulers and the faces of the story's antagonists.

Four of them are named. Kade Voss, "The Eye of the Market", watches the Neon Market through screens, drones and holograms. Rhea Calder, "The Iron Matron", runs the factory floor with machinery and brute force. Silas Wren, "The Whisper on the Rooftops", keeps the skyline from above. Dr. Maren Holt, "The Voice of Compliance", works in the undercity lab with gas and fog. Above them stands Overseer Halden Varr, "The Architect of Rust", who also founded the Rust and fights as the main boss in the Corporate Tower command chamber.

The neighbourhood answers every screen they put up.

lore.gddGap: The GDD lists five unit types but not how they relate on the ground. This ties them into one ladder (Grunts, Rangers, Breakers, Copper Fangs, Overseers) so levels and enemy writers can pace waves; the owner should confirm it.
lore.name: The Rust Ladder
lore.summary: A way to read the five Rust units as a ladder: Iron Line up front, Watchers and Breakers in support, Fangs and Overseers at the top.
lore.body:
Each district tends to open with the Iron Line, add Watchers on the rooftops and Breakers in the street, and finish with a Copper Fang or the district Overseer. The tougher the unit, the closer it sits to Overseer Varr.

The neighbourhood keeps score in its own way: every rung Zed knocks back is a corner, a court or a window that gets its music back.

lore.gddGap: The GDD gives the Rust's doctrine but no community reply. The tone rules say Rust copy is always answered or defaced by the neighbourhood, so this proposes a painted answer to the creed.
lore.name: The Wall Answers Back
lore.summary: Every time the Rust post their creed, someone paints over it with a line about looking out for each other.
lore.body:
Under a Rust notice, kids chalk in "Freedom is strength" and an arrow pointing to the food stall. Murals go back up a patch at a time. It never lasts long, but it is always there by morning.

It matches Zed's own belief: strength is protecting the people who give your life meaning.

lore.name: Street Weapons
lore.summary: From Level 2, Zed can crack open weapon boxes and pick up a baseball bat or a pipe to take on the Rust Grunts.
lore.body: Only two weapons exist for now, the baseball bat and the pipe. Zed breaks a box, picks the weapon up, carries it and swings with the same light and heavy buttons he already uses. Both hit harder than his heavy attack, but they wear out, so every swing counts.

lore.name: Baseball Bat
lore.summary: The quick weapon: a fast swing, short reach and ten hits of wear before it breaks.
lore.body:
Damage 20, with a 7 frame startup, 4 active and 16 recovery. Its hitbox is 64 wide, knockback is 400 and hitstun 26 frames. It lasts 10 hits, and a Grunt goes down in 2.

The heavy swing does 25 damage and costs 2 durability instead of 1. A heavy swing still goes through with 1 durability left, and the bat breaks afterwards.

lore.name: Pipe
lore.summary: The reach weapon: the longest hitbox in the game, a slower start and eight hits of wear.
lore.body:
Damage 24, with a 12 frame startup, 4 active and 20 recovery. Its hitbox is 84 wide, the longest in the game. Knockback is 360 and hitstun 28 frames. It lasts 8 hits, and a Grunt goes down in 2.

The heavy swing does 30 damage and costs 2 durability. Zed has to commit to the slower startup to get the reach.

lore.name: Weapon Box
lore.summary: One fixed box per level from Level 2, holding a bat or a pipe, breaking after 2 hits from Zed.
lore.body:
Each level from Level 2 has one weapon box in a fixed spot. What is inside is chosen by the level designer and is never random. Boxes do not respawn.

The box break animation is added separately.

lore.name: Worn Out, Dropped, Picked Up Again
lore.summary: Weapons break after a set number of hits, and Zed drops one if he is hit more than 3 times while carrying it.
lore.body:
When a weapon runs out of hits it breaks, a short break effect plays and Zed goes back to his fists. There is no drop button: the weapon falls on the 4th hit he takes. It lies on the floor, keeps its remaining durability, and Zed can pick it up again. Picking it up does not reset the hit count.

While Zed carries a weapon, the HUD shows its icon and remaining durability beside the health bar.

lore.name: The Throw
lore.summary: Zed can hurl a carried weapon; it spins through the air and hits the first Rust enemy in its path.
lore.body:
A throw does 15 damage with knockback 300 and 20 frames of hitstun. It travels at 480 pixels per second for up to 320 pixels and costs 2 durability.

If the weapon survives, it lands where it hit or at the end of its flight and Zed can pick it up again. With 2 durability or less, the throw still goes through and the weapon breaks when it lands.

lore.name: Boxes Left Behind the Shops
lore.summary: Where the weapon boxes come from: crates the neighbourhood tucked away behind the corner shops, for when the block needs them.
lore.body:
Nobody says who packed them. A bat from somebody's old pickup game, a length of pipe from a shuttered stall. The neighbourhood keeps looking out for each other, even after the Rust came through.

Zed does not fight for glory, so he borrows these only while they last.

enemies.gddGap: CANON/PROPOSED SPLIT: name, Level 1 mini-boss role, former dock worker backstory, gear and the five named moves are canon (lore item brick-dugan). Stats, telegraph timings, tier, look palette and the low-health trigger threshold are invented because the GDD gives no numbers. Tier 2 (the player's first major skill check, so above Breaker HP but below the Overseers).
enemies.name: "Brick" Dugan
enemies.description: A broad former dock worker recruited into the Rust, built like a human battering ram. Heavy black security vest with the Rust insignia, riot-control shoulder pads, reinforced forearm guards, steel-toe boots and a utility belt of restraints and radio gear. Boxy and symmetrical, slate and gunmetal tones, narrow cyan visor. Lore: brick-dugan.
enemies.behaviour: Slow but intimidating and easy to read. Walks Zed down, uses Brick Breaker Punch up close, Running Shoulder Charge along a lane from range, Ground Stomp when Zed is airborne or crowding him, and Grab and Wall Slam if Zed stays in melee range too long. Below 30 percent health (proposed threshold) he enters Rage Punch mode: one extra-heavy punch, still telegraphed. Takes an attacker slot before every move. Boss hitstun immunity so juggles cannot loop him.
enemies.telegraph: Brick Breaker Punch 650 ms: fist drawn back, shoulders squared. Running Shoulder Charge 800 ms: he lowers his shoulder and scrapes a boot, red ground strip along the lane. Ground Stomp 700 ms: knee lifts high, red circle under his boots. Grab and Wall Slam 600 ms: both arms open wide, red icon. Rage Punch 900 ms: longer wind-up with a held fist and a bigger red icon.
enemies.weakness: Dodge sideways out of the charge lane and he crashes into the arena wall, leaving a long recovery to punish. Jump the Ground Stomp, back-step the grab. Do not trade blows head-on: block the punch, then hit him in recovery. Teaches dodging as the first real skill check.

enemies.gddGap: CANON/PROPOSED SPLIT: name, Level 2 (Transit District) mini-boss role, former transit security officer, electrified baton, armoured trench coat, scanner visor, five named moves and the stun-mechanics role are canon (lore item railgun-royce). Stats, timings, tier, stun duration and Rail Trap layout are invented.
enemies.name: "Railgun" Royce
enemies.description: A former transit security officer in a long armoured trench coat, slate with gunmetal panels, carrying an electrified baton and wearing a scanner visor that glows cyan. Upright, symmetrical, boxy shoulders. Lore: railgun-royce.
enemies.behaviour: Mid-range controller who introduces stun. Opens with a Baton Combo, closes distance with a Charging Dash, answers a crowding Zed with Shockwave Slam, and lays Rail Trap electrified floor strips that block part of the lane for a few seconds (proposed 4 s). Taser Burst is a short-range stun shot. Being stunned briefly locks Zed's inputs (proposed 600 ms), never more, so the player learns to avoid rather than die to it. Takes an attacker slot before every move.
enemies.telegraph: Baton Combo 500 ms: baton raised and crackling. Charging Dash 650 ms: crouch with the visor flashing, red ground strip. Shockwave Slam 750 ms: baton planted overhead, red circle around him. Rail Trap 800 ms: he kneels and a cyan line marks the floor strip before it electrifies. Taser Burst 550 ms: arm extends, visor locks on with a red icon.
enemies.weakness: Stay off the marked Rail Trap strips and dodge the Taser Burst by moving out of line. Parry or jump the dash, then heavy-attack him in the long recovery after Shockwave Slam. Rewards reading the floor and the dodge.

enemies.gddGap: CANON/PROPOSED SPLIT: name, Level 3 (Industrial Zone) mini-boss role, chief enforcer to Rhea Calder, hydraulic work suit, industrial hammer, five named moves and the role of preparing players for Calder are canon (lore item crusher-kane). Stats, timings, tier and steam vent geometry are invented. Deliberately a slower, heavier version of the grunt's timing, foreshadowing Calder's 900 ms telegraphs.
enemies.name: "Crusher" Kane
enemies.description: Rhea Calder's chief enforcer in a bulky hydraulic work suit, slate with gunmetal pistons and steam pipes along the arms, swinging a huge industrial hammer. Visor slit glows cyan. Symmetrical, boxy and slow-moving. Lore: crusher-kane; serves rust-overseer-calder.
enemies.behaviour: Heavy slow bruiser who previews Calder. Hammer Slam is his main attack, Hook Chain Grab pulls Zed in from range, Furnace Kick is a short sweeping kick, Steam Vent Burst vents a cone of steam from the suit that leaves a hazard patch (proposed 3 s), Crushing Uppercut launches Zed upward if he is standing close. Slow movement, long recoveries. Takes an attacker slot before every move. Boss hitstun immunity.
enemies.telegraph: Hammer Slam 850 ms: hammer lifted overhead with a red ground circle. Hook Chain Grab 700 ms: chain whirls above his head and the hook flashes, red icon. Furnace Kick 600 ms: leg pulls back, steam hisses from the knee. Steam Vent Burst 900 ms: suit shakes and steam builds on the shoulders, red cone on the ground. Crushing Uppercut 750 ms: hammer swung low behind him, red strip in front.
enemies.weakness: Dodge out of the red circle and strike during the long Hammer Slam recovery. Break line of sight on the Hook Chain, stay out of steam patches. Back away from the uppercut and punish. Trains the player to wait for big telegraphs before Overseer Calder.

enemies.gddGap: CANON/PROPOSED SPLIT: name, Level 4 (Neon Market) mini-boss role, former hacker turned Rust cyber operative, holographic mask, portable drone pack, five named moves and the role of introducing Voss's deception mechanics are canon (lore item glitch). Stats, timings, tier, clone count and teleport rules are invented. Drones he launches reuse rust-voss-drone and his Hologram Duplicate reuses rust-hologram-decoy.
enemies.name: "Glitch"
enemies.description: A former hacker turned Rust cyber operative, thinner than other Rust units, slate uniform under a flickering holographic mask and a portable drone pack on his back with cyan indicator lights. Still symmetrical and boxy at the shoulders. Lore: glitch; previews rust-overseer-voss.
enemies.behaviour: Evasive deception fighter who keeps his distance. Drone Barrage launches a small volley of drones (reuses the Voss drone unit, proposed 2 at a time), Hologram Duplicate creates one decoy of himself that throws a weak punch (reuses the hologram decoy), Shock Disk Throw is a straight ranged projectile, Data Spike is a short ground line attack. Emergency Teleport triggers when Zed gets close or health drops past a threshold (proposed 50 percent): he blinks to the far side of the arena with a brief vulnerable pause on arrival. Takes an attacker slot before every move.
enemies.telegraph: Drone Barrage 700 ms: pack opens and lights blink, red icon above the pack. Hologram Duplicate 500 ms: mask flickers and the decoy shimmers into place. Shock Disk Throw 550 ms: disk spun up in his hand, red line of flight. Data Spike 600 ms: he crouches and a cyan line draws on the floor before the spike. Emergency Teleport 400 ms: mask static then a cyan flash, and a 700 ms vulnerable pause on arrival.
enemies.weakness: Pick out the real Glitch (the decoy's outline wobbles and it has no pack), dodge the disk line and punish him right after the teleport arrival. Breaking the drones with a quick combo keeps pressure off. Introduces the 'which one is real' skill before Overseer Voss.

enemies.gddGap: CANON/PROPOSED SPLIT: name, Level 5 (Skyline District) mini-boss role, Silas Wren's personal hunter, grapple launcher, lightweight armour, five named moves and the role of training vertical combat are canon (lore item raptor). Stats, timings, tier and the look (slate, light plating) are invented. Fast and fragile compared with Kane, mirroring Wren's 400 ms telegraphs.
enemies.name: "Raptor"
enemies.description: Silas Wren's personal hunter in lightweight slate armour with a shoulder-mounted grapple launcher, a swept-back visor and a narrow, agile frame. Cold hue, symmetrical, boxy plates kept light. Lore: raptor; serves rust-overseer-wren.
enemies.behaviour: Fast vertical attacker. Dive Kick drops from a jump onto Zed's position, Wall Bounce Strike rebounds off the arena edge into a diagonal strike, Grapple Pull yanks Zed a short way, Aerial Barrage is a flurry of kicks in the air, Falcon Drop is a high leap followed by a heavy slam on a marked spot. Often airborne, so ground-only attacks miss him. Takes an attacker slot before every move. Boss hitstun immunity.
enemies.telegraph: Dive Kick 450 ms: crouch and jump with a red ground marker where he will land. Wall Bounce Strike 500 ms: he skids toward the wall and flashes the visor. Grapple Pull 550 ms: launcher raised, a thin cyan cable line to Zed. Aerial Barrage 600 ms: he rises with legs pulled up, red icon overhead. Falcon Drop 800 ms: he leaps off-screen with a long shadow growing on the ground before the slam.
enemies.weakness: Anti-air hits and jump attacks catch him in the air, and the red ground marker shows exactly where to step away from. Dodge the cable line, then punish his landing recovery. Trains vertical awareness before Overseer Wren.

enemies.gddGap: CANON/PROPOSED SPLIT: name, Level 6 (Undercity) mini-boss role, failed chemical test subject of Dr. Holt, mutated physique, back chemical tanks, glowing green veins, five named moves and the area-denial role are canon (lore item holts-experiment-subject-88). Stats, timings, tier and hazard sizes are invented. Subject 88 is a person from Holt's experiments, not a monster: describe him with care, no gore. Green glow is canon; Overload Violet is reserved for phase-2 power glows and is not used here.
enemies.name: Dr. Holt's Experiment "Subject 88"
enemies.description: A hulking, hunched test subject from Dr. Holt's experiments, with a mutated physique, chemical tanks strapped to the back and glowing green veins along the arms and neck. Torn Rust-issue clothing hangs off the shoulders. Confused and in distress rather than cruel. Lore: holts-experiment-subject-88; ties to rust-overseer-holt.
enemies.behaviour: Area-denial bruiser. Toxic Breath is a short cone of gas that lingers, Acid Spit lobs a puddle at Zed's position (proposed 3 s), Frenzied Charge is a lane charge when he flares, Corrosion Slam is a heavy overhead strike that leaves a small puddle, Chemical Explosion bursts from the tanks in a ring at low health (proposed 40 percent) and is the only time he stops advancing. Hazards stay on the ground and slowly fade. Takes an attacker slot before every move.
enemies.telegraph: Toxic Breath 600 ms: chest swells and green mist leaks from the tanks. Acid Spit 650 ms: head tilts back, a green circle forms on the ground. Frenzied Charge 800 ms: he roars and the veins brighten, red lane strip. Corrosion Slam 750 ms: both fists raised, red circle. Chemical Explosion 1000 ms: tanks glow brighter and rattle, ring warning grows on the floor.
enemies.weakness: Keep moving: hazards punish standing still. Dodge the lane charge into the wall, then heavy-attack in recovery. Step out of the ring before the Chemical Explosion and hit him afterward. Rewards positioning and spacing.

enemies.gddGap: CANON/PROPOSED SPLIT: name, Level 7 (Rust Military Compound) mini-boss role, leader of the Copper Fangs, elite black armour, tactical shield, twin electrified gauntlets, five named moves (including Fang Protocol calling in Specialists) and the 'toughest non-boss enemy' claim are canon (lore item commander-atlas). Stats, timings, tier, Specialist count and phase thresholds are invented. Deliberately tuned above rust-copper-fang (140 HP) and below Overseers to honour 'toughest non-boss'.
enemies.name: Commander Atlas
enemies.description: The leader of the Copper Fangs: elite black armour with copper-toned gauntlets, a large tactical shield and twin electrified gauntlets, a hard symmetrical helmet with a narrow cyan visor. The sharpest, most composed Rust unit in the game. Lore: commander-atlas; leads rust-copper-fang units.
enemies.behaviour: Disciplined shield-and-gauntlet duelist. Shield Bash opens and breaks Zed's guard, Gauntlet Combo is a fast 3-hit string, Grapple Hook Pull yanks Zed in, Electric Counter is a stance that punishes mashed attacks while he holds the shield up, and Fang Protocol calls in Specialists (proposed 2 rust-copper-fang units, never more than 2 on screen, called once per phase). Below 50 percent health he drops the shield stance for faster gauntlet strings. Takes an attacker slot before every move. Boss hitstun immunity.
enemies.telegraph: Shield Bash 550 ms: shield pulled in, red ground strip in front. Gauntlet Combo 400 ms: gauntlets spark and cross in front of him, each hit has a short flash. Grapple Hook Pull 650 ms: launcher raised, cyan cable line shows the path. Electric Counter 500 ms: shield held up with crackling gauntlets, red shield-edge flash if Zed attacks into it. Fang Protocol 900 ms: he raises one fist and a signal flare pulses, Specialists arrive after 1200 ms.
enemies.weakness: Wait out the Electric Counter stance rather than mashing, dodge the cable line, then heavy-attack to break the shield. Parry the Gauntlet Combo's first hit to open a juggle. Defeating or avoiding the Specialists first reduces pressure. Rewards patience and parrying, the full toolkit of block, dodge, parry and combos.

enemies.gddGap: CANON/PROPOSED SPLIT: name, Level 8 (Corporate Tower) mini-boss role, experimental combat android protecting Varr, Rust insignia, chest energy core, five named moves, the phase-2 core overload (faster attacks, red laser barrage, explosive dash attacks) and its role as the final challenge before Varr are canon (lore item sentinel-x9). Stats, timings, tier, Self-Repair rate and phase threshold are invented. The GDD's red laser barrage conflicts with the owner decision that phase-2 power glows use Overload Violet and enemy bodies never use red: the barrage is drawn Overload Violet with a Telegraph Red ground warning (open question for the owner). It is a machine, so it is powered down rather than destroyed on defeat.
enemies.name: Sentinel-X9
enemies.description: An experimental corporate combat android, tall and perfectly symmetrical, with slate and steel plating, a Rust insignia on the chest plate and a round energy core glowing cyan in the chest. Visor slit cyan. In phase 2 the core overloads and glows Overload Violet with cracks of light along the plating. Lore: sentinel-x9; protects rust-halden-varr.
enemies.behaviour: Mechanical, rhythmic and precise. Laser Sweep arcs a beam across the lane from the eyes, Rocket Punch fires a fist forward in a straight line and it returns, Ground Pound is a heavy slam with a shockwave ring, Energy Shield blocks front hits until a heavy break, Self-Repair Mode rises when health is low and heals slowly while he is stationary (proposed 5 HP per second for up to 4 s, interruptible). Phase 2 (below 50 percent health): faster attacks, a Laser Sweep that becomes a laser barrage (multiple beams) and explosive dash attacks. Takes an attacker slot before every move. Boss hitstun immunity.
enemies.telegraph: Laser Sweep 700 ms: head turns, eyes charge cyan, red arc on the ground. Rocket Punch 600 ms: arm retracts with a whine, red lane strip. Ground Pound 800 ms: both fists rise overhead, red ring around him. Energy Shield 400 ms: core flares and a shield bubble forms. Self-Repair Mode 500 ms: panels open and green sparks. Phase 2 laser barrage 600 ms and explosive dash 450 ms (faster), each with a violet core pulse and red ground warning.
enemies.weakness: Heavy attacks break the Energy Shield, interrupt Self-Repair with a burst of damage before it heals, and dodge the lane strips. Phase 2 punishes standing still but its shorter pauses after the dash give a clear opening. A final test of block, dodge, parry and combos before Halden Varr.

enemies.gddGap: The GDD lists Rust Grunts, 'The Iron Line', for crowd control and frontline combat, but the Tier 0 rust-grunt is the only canon stat block. This is the Iron Line's crowd-control variant: a grunt that holds a line and sweeps a wide arc, so waves can pin the lane without adding a new silhouette. The base Iron Line unit remains rust-grunt (canon). FINAL BALANCE (tuned against the combat contract: Zed light 6-7, heavy 12, finisher 18 damage; grunt 30 HP / 8 damage / 450 ms telegraph as the Tier 0 anchor; every telegraph at least 300 ms): 36 HP is about 5 light hits, same damage as the grunt, 500 ms wind-up so the wide sweep reads one beat slower. Final.
enemies.name: Rust Iron Line Cordon
enemies.description: A Rust grunt of the Iron Line in cheap rust-coated slate plating, a plain steel helmet with a cyan visor and no personal marks, because the helmets hide who they are. Same boxy, symmetrical build as the grunt, with a gunmetal push-bar held across the chest.
enemies.behaviour: Moves in at grunt speed and stops at the front of the group to hold the lane, trying to pin Zed against his own crowd. Uses one wide sweep with the push-bar that shoves Zed back along the lane. Counts against the attacker cap like any other attacker, and never attacks from behind. When Zed gets too close or grabs too often it answers with the grunt Helmet Headbutt (short wind-up, brief stun) from the GDD Iron Line move list.
enemies.telegraph: 500 ms wind-up: both arms pull the bar to one side, the red telegraph icon pops above the head, the body tints red and the outline thickens. The sweep is wide, so the red ground arc shows its reach.
enemies.weakness: Low health and a short reach in depth. Step out of the lane (dodge) or block the shove, then punish in the recovery window. Heavy attacks from the side skip its guard-stance and juggle it clear of the line.
enemies.look: Grunt silhouette in rust-coated slate plating with a gunmetal push-bar across the chest; plain steel helmet, cyan visor.

moves.name: Rust Jab Combo
moves.gdd: GDD Iron Line move: quick 1-2-3 string, light damage.

moves.name: Helmet Headbutt
moves.gdd: GDD Iron Line move: short windup lunge, brief stun.

moves.name: Push-bar Sweep
moves.gdd: Wide lane-holding sweep. Not in the GDD; supports the GDD purpose line (crowd control, frontline combat).

enemies.gddGap: CANON/PROPOSED SPLIT: unit name, role line, lore, arena, phase triggers and named moves are canon (see moves[].canon and the cited chunks). Stats, all telegraph timings, tier placement and the visual look are proposed because the GDD gives no numbers or visuals (see proposedFields). The GDD defines Rust Bruisers, "The Breakers": massive shock troops on muscle stimulants (former criminals promised freedom for loyalty) for area denial, with three named moves: Gauntlet Smash, Rust Uppercut and Body Check. It gives no stats. The stat block and telegraph timings are proposed; the three moves are canon. Open question for the combat contract: ground bounce, block-break and super armour do not exist in the engine yet. Merged: replaces rust-enforcer. FINAL BALANCE (tuned against the combat contract: Zed light 6-7, heavy 12, finisher 18 damage; grunt 30 HP / 8 damage / 450 ms telegraph as the Tier 0 anchor; every telegraph at least 300 ms): 90 HP is about 5 heavy hits, 16 damage is two grunt hits, 700 ms wind-up and 1100 ms recovery give a big punish window. Final.
enemies.name: Rust Breaker
enemies.description: A hulking Rust Bruiser in heavily reinforced slate and steel plating, with a massive squared-off silhouette, a small helmet and a cyan visor. Cold, symmetrical and boxy; massive shock trooper enhanced with illegal muscle stimulants, built to crush resistance groups. A gunmetal brace on each forearm.
enemies.behaviour: Walks slowly straight at Zed, ignoring the circling rules, and takes an attacker slot when one is free. Plants its feet and slams both braces into the floor, leaving a short patch of rattled ground in front of it that Zed should stay out of for a moment (area denial). Long recovery after every slam. Cannot be juggled while winding up, so the player must dodge, not just mash. GDD move list. 1) Gauntlet Smash: downward smash with a reinforced gauntlet, medium startup, causes ground bounce, breaks player block, signature thud on impact (this is the slam above). 2) Rust Uppercut: a rising punch that launches Zed and works as an anti-air option; used when Zed jumps too often. 3) Body Check: a shoulder slam with plated armour, a short forward dash that knocks Zed back, can interrupt combos, and has super armour during the dash.
enemies.telegraph: 700 ms wind-up: both braces raised overhead, telegraph icon scaled 1.4 times and a large red ground danger ellipse at 30 percent alpha showing the slam area, per the heavy-enemy cue.
enemies.weakness: Big, slow and predictable. Dodge out of the red ellipse, then land a full combo in the long recovery. Heavy attacks stagger it; blocking works but the shove-back is large. Do not try to trade hits during the Body Check dash (super armour): sidestep it. Stop jumping in on it, or the Uppercut answers. Block does not hold against the Smash (it breaks block), so dodge it.
enemies.look: Hulking squared-off silhouette in heavy slate and steel plating, small helmet, cyan visor, gunmetal gauntlet brace on each forearm.

moves.name: Gauntlet Smash
moves.gdd: Downward smash with a reinforced gauntlet; medium startup, ground bounce, breaks player block, signature thud.

moves.name: Rust Uppercut
moves.gdd: Rising punch fuelled by stimulants; launches the player, anti-air option, used when the player jumps too often.

moves.name: Body Check
moves.gdd: Shoulder slam with plated armour; short forward dash, knocks player back, can interrupt combos, super armour during the dash.

enemies.gddGap: CANON/PROPOSED SPLIT: unit name, role line, lore, arena, phase triggers and named moves are canon (see moves[].canon and the cited chunks). Stats, all telegraph timings, tier placement and the visual look are proposed because the GDD gives no numbers or visuals (see proposedFields). The GDD defines Rust Rangers, "The Watchers": agile units with taser rifles, batons and tracking visors that scan heat signatures, for long-range harassment, pursuit and reconnaissance, with two named moves: Taser Shot and Baton Strike. It gives no stats. Stats are proposed. Conflict to resolve: the GDD gives the Baton Strike a "very quick startup", but the readability rule keeps telegraphs at 300 ms or more, so this entry uses 350 ms. Merged: replaces rust-dart-marksman and rust-baton-scout. FINAL BALANCE (tuned against the combat contract: Zed light 6-7, heavy 12, finisher 18 damage; grunt 30 HP / 8 damage / 450 ms telegraph as the Tier 0 anchor; every telegraph at least 300 ms): 28 HP (fragile, rewards closing in), 7 damage per bolt, 650 ms taser wind-up, 350 ms baton wind-up. Final.
enemies.name: Rust Watcher
enemies.description: A lean, agile Rust Ranger in a slate uniform with a gunmetal taser rifle, a baton at the belt and a wide tracking visor with a cyan scan line. Symmetrical and boxy, but lighter than the grunt.
enemies.behaviour: Stays at range, strafing along the far side of the arena and following Zed with its visor. Fires a single slow taser bolt along the lane when it holds an attacker slot, then relocates. If Zed closes in it backs off, and only swings the baton when cornered. A hunter built to harass rebels at range and chase them down. GDD move list. Taser Shot: a quick electric bolt, light damage, brief stun on hit, used constantly to harass and to encourage Zed to close distance. Baton Strike: a fast electrified-baton hit with very quick startup that interrupts combos, used when Zed gets too close. Lore: trained to track rebels through alleyways and rooftops; the visor scans heat signatures, so hiding barely works.
enemies.telegraph: 650 ms wind-up for the taser: rifle raised, a cyan scan line draws along the floor toward Zed, and the red telegraph icon pops above the head. The bolt is slow enough to sidestep. The baton swing uses a 350 ms wind-up with the standard cues.
enemies.weakness: Low health. Sidestep out of the lane to dodge, then close the gap; juggle routes that carry Zed across the arena reach it fast. Blocking the bolt is also possible but eats a chip of damage.
enemies.look: Lean slate uniform, gunmetal taser rifle, baton at the belt, wide tracking visor with a cyan scan line; lighter boxy build than the grunt.

moves.name: Taser Shot

enemies.name: Rust Grunt
enemies.description: The one enemy type the GDD asks for first: a Rust security officer in a slate uniform with a steel helmet and a cyan visor. Symmetrical, boxy and cold, a sharp contrast to Zed's warm, rounded look. Lore: the Rust strip recruits of their names and give them serial numbers, so the helmets hide who is under them on purpose; many were ordinary citizens coerced or manipulated into service.
enemies.behaviour: Idles briefly after spawn, then chases Zed. Closes the lane gap first, and starts a strike once in range. At most two grunts may attack at once (attacker cap); the rest circle at a distance in neutral colours until a slot frees up. GDD move list (Iron Line grunts): Rust Jab Combo, a quick 1-2-3 punch string of light damage, used to interrupt the player and often done in groups to create pressure; and Helmet Headbutt, a sudden forward lunge with a reinforced helmet, short wind-up, brief stun, used when Zed is too close or grabs too often. The Tier 0 engine implements the single strike only; the jab combo and headbutt are later-tier additions to gruntData.js and need the combat contract to support multi-hit strings and a stun hit.
enemies.telegraph: 450 ms wind-up: three-frame anticipation pose with the arm pulled back, the red telegraph icon pops above the head, the body tints red and the outline thickens. Then a quick 250 ms strike and a 700 ms recovery where it is open to a counter.
enemies.weakness: Low health and a slow recovery. Dodge or block the telegraphed strike, then punish during recovery with a light combo.
enemies.look: Slate uniform, steel helmet, cyan visor, cheap oxidized plating kept to cold slate tones; boxy and symmetrical, no personal marks (serial-number recruits).
